newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine auto part makers seek relief.
newsitem.headline: Philippine auto part makers seek relief.

text.p: Philippine automotive parts makers said on Friday they wanted a ten-year delay in the total liberalisation of the industry up to the year 2010.

The sector was not ready for the planned complete liberalization of the industry by the year 2000, the Association of Consolidated Automotive Parts Producers Inc (ACAPP) said in a letter to Trade and Industry Undersecretary Melito Salazar.

ACAPP president George Lim said local content and foreign exchange requirements for completely-knocked-down (CKD) parts should stay until the year 2010 to give enough time for local component makers to adjust.

Automotive assemblers are required to achieve a local content of at least 50 percent. They will also have to earn much of their foreign exchange costs for their imported parts from the export of locally-made components.
"There is no need to accelerate liberalisation," Lim said. -- Manila newsroom (632) 841-8937
